purpose: Determine whether the repeated local-pass/whole-episode-degradation pattern is driven primarily by cumulative surface contamination, repeated plan-purpose serialization, continuity debt, or a mixture, using only sealed historical outputs.

hypotheses.H_W1_CUMULATIVE_CONTAMINATION: Absolute surface-contamination metrics increase or remain pathologically high across episode progression and predict whole-episode craft degradation.
hypotheses.H_W2_PLAN_PURPOSE_AMPLIFICATION: Repeated sequence/scene plan-purpose serialization accumulates approximately with member-scene count and accounts for a material share of whole-episode surface length.
hypotheses.H_W3_CONTINUITY_DEBT: State/temporal/logistical/relationship violations concentrate in later scene indices or after repeated state transitions.

analysis_plan.per_work: Compute scene-level time series and early/middle/late tercile summaries.
analysis_plan.trend: Estimate robust slope vs scene index for contamination and continuity metrics.
analysis_plan.cross_case: Compare direction and magnitude across the three sealed historical cases.
analysis_plan.no_causal_overclaim: A positive slope is diagnostic association, not proof of causality.

forbidden_actions: no use of results to reinterpret a sealed PASS/FAIL verdict
next_after_diagnostic: Use the dominant signature only to design a completely fresh prospective intervention and preregister it before new outputs.
